messages:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — NCCL communicator timeout detected on cluster-gpu-5 (tp group: model-infer-768)

Maya Chen: I'm on it. Seeing a spike in 500/502 errors from the realtime inference fleet and a cluster node flapping.

Maya Chen: quick summary: multiple containers restarting, CUDA OOMs in logs, ncclCommReduceScatter timed out repeatedly. Latency p99 jumped from ~80ms -> 2.1s for some routes.

Samir Patel: oncall acked. samir here, I'm pulling logs and will coordinate mitigation. @Maya can you paste the exact pod errors?

Maya Chen: paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T06:12:32Z] model-infer-768-0 stderr: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: allocating 536870912 bytes
[2026-03-15T06:12:32Z] model-infer-768-0 stderr: NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommReduceScatter failed : Timeout
[2026-03-15T06:12:33Z] model-infer-768-0 stderr: NCCL INFO communicator 0x7f9c1234 unrecoverable
[2026-03-15T06:12:34Z] kernel: NMI watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
```

Erin Zhao: noted. Which deployment topology is affected? tp or pp? looks like TP with 4 ranks.

Maya Chen: tensor-parallel 4-way, serving runtime used multi-gpu communicator pinned across 4 GPUs on node cluster-gpu-5. Node flapped (OOM -> container restart -> communicator enter bad state). We have downstream enqueue backlog.

ops-runbook-bot: Recommended mitigation steps: 1) Fail traffic to fallback single-gpu variant 2) Drain affected node 3) Restart runtime processes 4) Collect nccl debug dump

Samir Patel: starting step 1: switching routing to fallback variant. Command I ran:
```
redwood traffic swap --from model-infer-768:tp4 --to model-infer-768:single-gpu --region us-west2
```

Samir Patel: traffic swap submitted, watching rollout. @Maya can you start draining cluster-gpu-5?

Maya Chen: cordoning + draining now.
```
kubectl cordon node/cluster-gpu-5
kubectl drain node/cluster-gpu-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Maya Chen: drain in progress. Some pods stuck in Terminating due to NCCL cleanup. I'll do a graceful kill of the runtime to trigger restart.

Maya Chen: killing runtime container on the node (runtime = redwood-inferd)
```
ssh root@cluster-gpu-5
systemctl restart redwood-inferd || docker restart $(docker ps -q --filter name=redwood-inferd)
```

Samir Patel: while that runs, I'm collecting nccl debug logs and GPU health
```
nvmltool -q --dumps
cat /var/log/redwood/inferd/nccl_debug.log | tail -n 200
```

Samir Patel: found repeated errors like "cudaLaunchKernel failed" and "ncclCommInitRank returned error Unimplemented"

Liam O'Connor: good catch. If communicator init fails post-restart, we need to ensure the kv-store of rank assignments is cleaned. On the runtime side we can force a fresh rendezvous by bumping job run_id.

Maya Chen: traffic swap completed: 100% -> single-gpu variant. Observed immediate drop in 500s on API gateway.

Maya Chen: metrics: affected routes ~models/compl-gen and models/summarize. Peak error rate: 4.3% of requests in the window (00:06:00 to 00:18:00 UTC). Estimated impacted customers: 5 paid customers with heavy tails; internal SLOs degraded but degradations are isolated thanks to fallback.

Samir Patel: cordon+drain done. runtime restarted. I'm re-provisioning communicators by bumping model-infer-768 tp variant (but traffic is already on single-gpu). Logs show no immediate OOM after restart.

Erin Zhao: do we have reason to suspect NVLINK hardware issue or purely software NCCL bug? Any recent driver/kernel updates on that node?

Maya Chen: kernel was updated a week ago but node passed post-update smoke. GPU firmware same as fleet. I see nvlink retries in dmesg but not a clear hardware ECC error.

Samir Patel: given the evidence (timeout + communicator unrecoverable on container restarts), plan:
- keep traffic on single-gpu fallback (rollback if needed)
- repro the issue on a staging host by simulating load and multi-gpu TP4
- collect full nccl debug + cuda memstats
- optionally upgrade NCCL runtime on that node to a newer tested build (coordinate maintenance)

Liam O'Connor: I'm volunteering to own the follow-up. I'll coordinate a staging repro and NCCL kernel tests. Postmortem owner: Liam.

Maya Chen: paging context for handoff: Samir you're taking next shift; handing over with current state:
- mitigations applied: traffic routed to fallback, node drained and runtime restarted
- impact: 5 customers affected briefly, <30min customer-impact window, peak 4.3% error rate on those routes, p99 latency for fallback up ~30ms
- logs collected: /var/log/redwood/inferd/nccl_debug.log, gpu nvml dumps, kube pod describe outputs
- next actions: repro in staging, run nccl test-suite, schedule maintenance window to upgrade nccl/driver on node if repro succeeds

Samir Patel: acked. I'll monitor for 2 hours and start a staging repro. If we see recurrence on other nodes I'll escalate to infra for hardware rotation.

Maya Chen: creating incident ticket and linking customers for follow-up. Estimated severity: Sev2 (partial but contained customer impact).

ops-runbook-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0315-214777. Assigned: Liam O'Connor (postmortem), Samir Patel (monitoring), Maya Chen (on-scene).

Liam O'Connor: I'll schedule the repro and add test matrix (NCCL 2.16 vs 2.18, driver 530.x vs 535.x, kernel 5.15 vs 6.1) and capture nvlink stress results.

Erin Zhao: please include the runtime version and the exact model shard config in the postmortem. Also capture a snapshot of config for traffic manager rules (so we can replay rollback steps).

Maya Chen: adding follow-ups to incident ticket and will attach logs. Handoff complete, taking down monitoring to let Samir lead.

Samir Patel: taking over. Ping me if errors reappear: @samir

Maya Chen: thanks team :thumbsup:

infra-bot: :wave: automated note: Next 1h monitoring alert group created. If the single-gpu fallback sees abnormal latency > 500ms for p95 for >=5m, auto-escalate to oncall-sre.

— end of thread —
